facts.label: Suspicious message received
facts.help: An unexpected message asks for an unusual action.

facts.label: Sender identity mismatch
facts.help: The actual sender or reply address differs from the claimed identity.

facts.label: Suspicious destination
facts.help: The link destination has been flagged or does not match the claimed service. Do not open it to check.

facts.label: Credentials entered on suspect page
facts.help: The user reports entering a password into the page linked by this message.

facts.label: Attachment or downloaded file executed
facts.help: The user ran a file associated with the suspect message.

facts.label: Credible malware alert
facts.help: Endpoint protection reported a malicious file or process; record the alert separately.

facts.label: Unexpected process observed
facts.help: An unexpected process is linked to the alert or reported event.

facts.label: Unexpected file encryption
facts.help: Files changed unexpectedly and cannot be opened; normal authorized encryption is excluded.

facts.label: Ransom demand present
facts.help: A demand for payment or extortion message is present.

facts.label: Security controls disabled unexpectedly
facts.help: Security software or logging was disabled without an approved change.

facts.label: Unauthorized persistence found
facts.help: An unapproved startup item, scheduled task or service is linked to suspicious activity.

facts.label: Unusual repeated login failures
facts.help: Failures materially exceed the normal baseline for the same account or service.

facts.label: Unrecognized login source
facts.help: The source is not recognized after checking normal access patterns.

facts.label: Success follows suspicious failures
facts.help: The same account has a successful login correlated with the unusual failures.

facts.label: Anomalous successful login
facts.help: A successful login is outside the usual device, time or location pattern.

facts.label: User denies the login
facts.help: The account owner confirms they did not perform this particular successful login.

facts.label: Privileged account affected
facts.help: The affected identity has administrator or equivalent elevated permissions.

facts.label: Unexpected repeated MFA prompts
facts.help: The user received authentication approval prompts they did not initiate.

facts.label: Unexpected MFA prompt approved
facts.help: The user approved one of those unsolicited prompts.

facts.label: Unusual outbound transfer volume
facts.help: Outbound volume materially exceeds the expected baseline for this asset.

facts.label: Transfer destination unapproved
facts.help: The external destination is not approved for the observed data transfer.

facts.label: Sensitive data accessed before transfer
facts.help: Logs correlate access to sensitive data with the unusual transfer.

facts.label: Credible data loss prevention alert
facts.help: A DLP alert identifies a suspect data transfer requiring review.

facts.label: Unusual inbound traffic volume
facts.help: Requests or traffic materially exceed the expected baseline.

facts.label: Service unavailable or degraded
facts.help: Users or health checks confirm a current service impact.

facts.label: Traffic from many sources
facts.help: The abnormal traffic is distributed across many apparent sources.

facts.label: Several hosts affected
facts.help: The same incident has correlated evidence on more than one host.

facts.label: Critical business asset affected
facts.help: The organization classifies the affected system as operationally critical.

facts.label: Sensitive information involved
facts.help: The affected asset or account handles sensitive information.

facts.label: Active spread observed
facts.help: Correlated evidence indicates the same activity is spreading now.

facts.label: Known usable isolated backup
facts.help: An isolated backup exists and its usability is known; recovery still requires approval.

facts.label: Material business disruption
facts.help: The event prevents an important business activity from operating normally.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-61 Revision 3
sources.scope: Incident analysis, prioritization, response and recovery; conceptual basis, not the exact project rules.

sources.title: CISA StopRansomware Guide
sources.scope: Ransomware response: coordinated isolation, preserving evidence and recovery planning.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1566 Phishing
sources.scope: Malicious messages, links, attachments and correlated execution.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1110 Brute Force
sources.scope: Repeated authentication attempts; project uses a qualitative local baseline.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
sources.scope: Outbound traffic anomalies correlated with data access; does not prove that every transfer uses C2.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1498 Network Denial of Service
sources.scope: Network traffic used to reduce service availability.

sources.title: SWI-Prolog HTTP server documentation
sources.scope: Prolog ecosystem reference; this project uses a Python local HTTP adapter and a SWI-Prolog subprocess.

sources.title: Project triage policy version 1
sources.scope: Author-designed conjunctions, priorities and follow-up actions. Not an official standard or expert-validated scoring system.

rules.explanation: The reported message and identity mismatch support suspected phishing.
A suspect message links to a suspect destination.
Credentials were supplied through a suspected phishing route.
Execution following suspected phishing requires malware investigation.
A credible endpoint alert supports suspected malware.
An unexpected process plus unauthorized persistence warrants investigation.
Unexpected encryption together with a ransom demand supports suspected ransomware.
Unexpected encryption and suspected malware support a ransomware hypothesis.
Repeated failures from an unrecognized source support an authentication attack hypothesis.
Success following correlated suspicious failures supports suspected account compromise.
An anomalous successful login denied by the owner warrants compromise investigation.
Exposed credentials create a suspected compromise risk even if subsequent use is unconfirmed.
Approving an unsolicited prompt supports an account compromise hypothesis.
Correlated sensitive data access and unusual unapproved outbound transfer support suspected data theft.
A credible data loss alert and unapproved destination support investigation of data theft.
Distributed abnormal traffic coincides with an availability impact.
Malware indicators occur on multiple correlated hosts.
Suspected phishing requires analyst triage.
An authentication attack hypothesis requires analyst triage.
This suspected incident category receives high priority under project policy.

This suspected incident category receives high priority under project policy.
Suspected ransomware receives the highest project priority.
An affected privileged identity increases potential impact.
Suspected data theft involving sensitive information is escalated.
Availability loss involving a critical asset is escalated.
Multi-host malware with observed spread requires urgent coordination.
High-priority incident plus material disruption is escalated.
Retain the original message and headers; avoid interacting with its links or attachments.
Ask the identity administrator to restrict affected access, revoke sessions and reset credentials from a trusted device; review MFA and account changes.
Have authorized responders coordinate network isolation of affected devices while preserving evidence.
Have authorized responders coordinate network isolation of affected devices while preserving evidence.
Record timestamps, affected assets and original alerts; preserve relevant logs with an evidence handling record.
Record timestamps, affected assets and original alerts; preserve relevant logs with an evidence handling record.
Record timestamps, affected assets and original alerts; preserve relevant logs with an evidence handling record.
Notify the incident lead promptly and coordinate operational decisions with the affected service owners.
Ask authorized responders to validate and restrict the suspect transfer, preserve transfer logs and assess the data involved.
Coordinate with the network team and service provider to validate the traffic and apply approved availability protections.
After containment and investigation, validate isolated backups and plan an approved clean recovery.
Escalate the absence of a known usable backup to the recovery lead; assess recovery options before any destructive action.
Investigate the disabled controls and associated changes; restore protection with responder approval.
